correctness.rationale: The finite Heawood incidence graph is defined by seven explicit Fano triples. The component-coloring lemma bijectively enumerates all ternary functions by exactly 16384 zero sets and 2^c flips, with exact neighborhood tests, obtaining coefficients 868,168,42,28,2 at weights 8,9,10,11,14. Independent exhaustive C++ testing of all 4782969 ternary labelings reproduces every coefficient and the point-zero split. The automorphism group proof enumerates all 168 line-preserving point permutations and extends by explicit duality to all 336 graph automorphisms; exact orbit enumeration checks nine orbit sizes summing to 868. All proof quantifiers concern a 14-vertex graph.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the unique cubic girth-six cage and a canonical finite projective-plane incidence graph. Counting *all* color-independent rainbow dominating placements and their nine symmetry types materially refines the scalar optimization parameter: it identifies a noncontiguous feasible-weight spectrum and the complete geometry of optimal configurations. The vertex-cut component decomposition also gives an exact structural mechanism behind the census. The graph is naturally motivated rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; no infinite-family extension is claimed.
